newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deutsche Telekom says may mull HK, S'pore listing.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom says may mull HK, S'pore listing.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG may consider listing its shares in Singapore or Hong Kong one year after listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Ron Sommer, chief executive officer of Deutsche Telekom, told a news conference on Friday.
"The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) is the most important exchange in Asia," Sommer said.
"If the demand is heavy, listing (of shares) one year later in Singapore or Hong Kong is being considered," he said.
The German telecommunications giant is due to float its stocks in Europe and the United States on November 18 and in Tokyo one day later.
Deutsche Telekom board members, including Sommer, are travelling to 30 cities in 17 countries around the world in a roadshow aimed at wooing investors to buy the company's shares.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who arrived in Tokyo on Thursday, is also helping to promote sales of Deutsche Telekom shares.
Kohl was to visit the Tokyo Stock Exchange later on Friday.
Sommer said Deutsche Telekom was able to offer discounts of up to 35 percent for big customers starting from Friday, having obstained a green light from the European Commission earlier this year.
